quests.question: Try not to _____ on past mistakes. Look ahead instead.
quests.explanation: 'Dwell on' means to think or talk too much about something. Example: 'Don't dwell on it.'

quests.question: If this fails, we can always _____ back on our savings.
quests.explanation: 'Fall back on' means to use something as a backup. Example: 'He fell back on his degree.'

quests.question: The team has come _____ a serious problem with funding.
quests.explanation: 'Come up against' means to meet a difficulty. Example: 'We came up against strong rivals.'

quests.question: We need to cut _____ on spending this year.
quests.explanation: 'Cut back on' means to reduce something. Example: 'I've cut back on coffee.'

quests.question: He backed _____ of the deal at the last minute.
quests.explanation: 'Back out of' means to decide not to do something you agreed to do.

quests.question: Can you stand _____ for me while I'm on leave?
quests.explanation: 'Stand in for' means to do someone's job for a short time. Example: 'She stood in for him.'

quests.question: She decided to pass _____ the offer. It wasn't right for her.
quests.explanation: 'Pass up' means to not take an opportunity. Example: 'I couldn't pass up the chance.'

quests.question: I didn't like him at first, but I've really taken _____ him.
quests.explanation: 'Take to' someone means to start liking them. Example: 'The kids took to the dog.'

quests.question: I can _____ by with basic Spanish while I'm travelling.
quests.explanation: 'Get by' means to manage with little. Example: 'We can get by on bread and cheese.'

quests.question: A thief _____ off with her laptop while she was queuing.
quests.explanation: 'Make off with' means to steal something and leave quickly. Example: 'He made off with my bag.'

quests.question: Hold _____ to your ticket; you'll need it later.
quests.explanation: 'Hold on to' means to keep something safe. Example: 'Hold on to the receipt.'

quests.question: They spent hours trying to _____ out an agreement.
quests.explanation: 'Thrash out' means to discuss something at length until you agree.

quests.question: She's trying to _____ up support for her local charity.
quests.explanation: 'Drum up' means to create interest or support. Example: 'We drummed up business.'

quests.question: My cousin roped me _____ helping at the school fair.
quests.explanation: 'Rope someone into' means to persuade them to join something. Example: 'I got roped into it.'

quests.question: Let's wait and see how things _____ out.
quests.explanation: 'Pan out' means to develop or turn out. Example: 'It didn't pan out as expected.'

quests.question: The new boss plans to _____ up the whole department.
quests.explanation: 'Shake up' means to make big changes to an organisation. Example: 'They shook up the team.'

quests.question: Don't let them _____ you off with excuses.
quests.explanation: 'Fob off' means to deceive someone with an excuse. Example: 'They fobbed me off.'

quests.question: You can bank _____ me to be there on time.
quests.explanation: 'Bank on' means to rely on something. Example: 'Don't bank on good weather.'

quests.question: I don't agree, but I'll _____ along for now.
quests.explanation: 'Play along' means to pretend to agree. Example: 'She played along with the joke.'

quests.question: She's quick to _____ up on small changes in people's moods.
quests.explanation: 'Pick up on' means to notice something. Example: 'He picked up on her tone.'

quests.question: He could _____ off the capitals of every European country.
quests.explanation: 'Reel off' means to say a long list quickly from memory. Example: 'She reeled off the names.'

quests.question: I need to _____ up on my French before the trip.
quests.explanation: 'Brush up on' means to improve a skill you haven't used for a while.

quests.question: Why don't you _____ around after the party and help us tidy?
quests.explanation: 'Stick around' means to stay somewhere a little longer. Example: 'Stick around for dinner.'

quests.question: I always _____ up the twins' names. They look so alike.
quests.explanation: 'Mix up' means to confuse two things or people. A 'mix-up' is a mistake.

quests.question: The roof could _____ in under so much snow.
quests.explanation: 'Cave in' means to fall inward. It also means to give in under pressure.

quests.question: I refuse to _____ out another fifty pounds for a ticket.
quests.explanation: 'Fork out' means to pay money, often unwillingly. Example: 'I forked out for repairs.'

quests.question: The wind began to _____ off in the evening.
quests.explanation: 'Ease off' means to become less strong. Example: 'The rain eased off at six.'

quests.question: After the success, the company decided to _____ out into new markets.
quests.explanation: 'Branch out' means to start doing something new. Example: 'She branched out into travel.'

quests.question: Many firms _____ in on the popularity of video games.
quests.explanation: 'Cash in on' means to profit from something. Example: 'They cashed in on the craze.'

quests.question: He began to _____ off during the long speech.
quests.explanation: 'Drift off' means to fall asleep gently. Example: 'I drifted off in the sun.'
